newsitem.title: FRANCE: European Union returns to grain subsidies.
newsitem.headline: European Union returns to grain subsidies.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday reverted to granting subsidies to its grain exporters for the first time in more than a year.
Subsidies had been suspended and the EU even imposed a prohibitive export tax for a while when the global market tightened and grain stocks fell to 20-year lows.
But several regions including the EU this year reported bumper harvests. A decision to return to subsidies was made during the weekly EU grain auction, to dispose of the larger-than-expected crop.
The EU may have a record grain harvest of up to 200 million tonnes this year, up more than 10 percent from 1995. Bigger crops have also been reported in Australia and China.
Wheat prices peaked near $300 per tonne in April, before sliding to the present $160 as the bigger harvests rolled in.
